I defined the evidence and decision boundaries for Helio Start from signup through the first paid month. I kept admission routing, pre-admission assistance, post-admission support, activation, and first-paid evidence distinct; pushed for the connector-access check when credential failures were obscuring setup fit; and framed the May decision around what the evidence could support. sent_emails.subject: December 10 board operating segment — pre-read
sent_emails.body:
Tomás —

# December 10 board operating segment — pre-read

## Page 1 — Opening frame
This pre-read presents four separate operating-evidence lanes: Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls. Each lane has its own denominator, complete outcome window, supported interpretation, and exclusions. The lanes must not be combined into one growth number or used to imply unsupported revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast conclusions.

---

## Page 2 — Helio Start
The mature packet contains 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows: 61 paid-active, 11 canceled, six past due, and four on billing hold. The cohort produced $95,420 in gross billed cash and $89,110 in refund-adjusted collected cash. Account-level support effort was 20 minutes at the median and 70 minutes at the 90th percentile. Seven accounts exceeded 90 minutes, all involving external-authority or ownership assistance. No manual-billing, import, migration, or agency case entered the admitted path.

Priya’s December 3 decision is to keep Helio Start as a bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026, with no paid-acquisition test, pipeline target, or forecast credit. A capped paid-acquisition proposal may be reopened only after two consecutive mature cohorts each have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes and no unsupported case enters the admitted path. Any proposal would still require separate budget approval.

The decision uses the evidence as a combined operating packet: complete day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort. The 61 paid-active count and $89,110 in refund-adjusted collected cash are useful mature-cohort evidence, but they are not scalable acquisition economics, pipeline, forecast credit, or a one-number conversion gate.

---

## Page 3 — Retained-mid Expansion Assist
Across the two bounded pilots’ closed, complete 45-day windows, 43 actual exposures produced 13 help-or-options requests and nine expansions. There was no randomized control, so the evidence is descriptive rather than causal.

The cohort definitions also differed: the requirement that the product-visible usage ceiling be newly crossed within the prior 14 days applied only to the second cohort, while 18 of the first pilot’s 30 exposures had an older ceiling event. Current-state safeguards applied, but the observed outcomes do not establish causal lift.

Expansion Assist remains a narrow, behavior-based, state-specific retained-mid operating lane. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses a commercial prompt. The lane remains outside pipeline, revenue commitments, forecast credit, broad-rollout claims, and Helio Start economics.

---

## Page 4 — Pricing-page path quality
The completed Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test covered 3,286 organic pricing-page sessions: 1,639 control and 1,647 treatment. Among Helio Start eligibility-flow starts, unsupported-condition route-outs fell from 38 of 344 control starts, or 11.0%, to 25 of 352 treatment starts, or 7.1% — a 35.7% relative reduction.

Eligible-workspace admission completion was 43.8% in control and 44.1% in treatment. Account-level support time at the 90th percentile was 71 minutes in control and 74 minutes in treatment. The direction held in all three weekly cohorts and the stabilization cohort. No unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change occurred, so the attribution check was clean. The result cleared the predeclared path-quality threshold and both guardrails.

The path-separated design has completed its rollout to 100% of organic traffic, and the control has been retired. Existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing events continue to populate without a taxonomy change. The supported interpretation is fewer unsupported self-serve starts and improved funnel quality, not revenue lift, paid-acquisition economics, pipeline, forecast credit, or changed eligibility.

---

## Page 5 — System controls
The certified October 1–31 CS auto-nudge packet covers 1,026 unique decisions. Forty-one produced visible field-specific holds, and 985 proceeded or were suppressed using current state. There was no governed-field disagreement and no customer correction. No held or suppressed record received adjacent lifecycle messaging that assumed eligibility, and no rollback was used.

This evidence supports system-control performance only: required holds remained visible, otherwise decisions proceeded or were suppressed using current state, governed views stayed aligned, adjacent messaging respected the state, and no rollback was required. It does not establish revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or customer-growth impact.

---

## Page 6 — Claims-and-exclusions matrix

| Evidence lane | Supported claim | Required exclusions |
|---|---|---|
| Helio Start | Among 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows, 61 are paid-active; refund-adjusted collected cash is $89,110; account-level support effort is 20 minutes at the median and 70 minutes at the 90th percentile; the channel remains organic through March 31, 2026 | Seven accounts exceeded 90 support minutes, all involving external-authority or ownership assistance; no paid-acquisition test, pipeline target, or forecast credit; reopening requires two consecutive mature cohorts each below 5%, no unsupported admitted case, and separate budget approval |
| Retained-mid Expansion Assist | Across complete 45-day windows, 43 actual exposures produced 13 help-or-options requests and nine expansions | Descriptive, not causal; no randomized control; 18 first-pilot exposures had an older usage-ceiling event; no broad rollout, causal lift, pipeline, revenue commitment, forecast credit, or Helio Start claim |
| Pricing-page path quality | The test produced a 35.7% relative reduction in unsupported-condition route-outs, passed both guardrails, had a clean attribution check, and completed a 100% organic rollout | Supports fewer unsupported-path starts only; no revenue lift, paid-acquisition economics, pipeline, forecast, eligibility change, or cross-lane growth claim |
| System controls | The October packet supports visible field-specific holds, current-state decisions, governed-field agreement, adjacent-message alignment, no customer correction, and no rollback | System-control performance only; no revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or customer-growth interpretation |

The four lanes remain separate. Their denominators and outcome windows are not interchangeable, and they must not be combined into one growth number.

Riley

docs.title: Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine
docs.body:
# Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine

## 1) Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise
- Helio Start is the working name for the sub-50-seat motion.
- It is not a cheap plan or launch promise.
- Eligibility, refusal rules, instrumentation, lifecycle paths, and support boundaries need to be ready before the name implies anything customer-facing or launch-like.

## 2) Measurement method
- Baseline uses activation definition v3: completed first integration plus at least one in-product event within the first 14 days.
- Keep 75-200-seat paid accounts as the separate mid-seg v2 comparison cut.
- Show the 50-75 seat band separately rather than folding it into mid-seg.

## 3) Baseline finding
- Under-50 accounts with simple deployment shape and a first integration in the first week behave near the current mid-seg+ target range.
- Under-50 accounts that need permissions, import help, billing exceptions, or migration support lag by more than 15 points.
- The 50-75 seat band again reads closer to starter behavior than retained mid-seg behavior.
- The useful signal is deployment and admin complexity, not a blanket seat-count verdict.

## 4) Eligibility and refusal-rule implications
- Favor under-50 accounts with simple deployment shape and first-week first integration in the first eligibility model.
- Treat permissions, import help, billing exceptions, and migration support as June refusal risks rather than default offer mechanics.
- Keep pricing-page or public-surface implications out until the operating-model boundaries are answered.

## 5) Open questions for lifecycle, instrumentation, support, and engineering sizing
- Lifecycle: which existing product-event emails can be adapted safely, and which branches would create premature support promises?
- Instrumentation: what tracking and reporting gaps need to close to keep the eligibility cuts readable?
- Support: what handoff rules are acceptable without quietly creating human-help expectations?
- Engineering sizing: what would it take to support permissions, imports, billing exceptions, or migrations later, without implying a Q3 build commitment now?

Q1 Growth operating review — January 31

Decision method
Denominators and effect size come before conclusions. We do not ship at first significance; the stabilization cohort rule still applies. Owen and Ines are lane maintainers, not a central approval queue.

Activation
Prior cohort activation is 135 of 236 (57.2%). Current cohort activation is 136 of 220 (61.8%). Standardizing the current stratum-specific rates to the prior integration-at-signup mix gives approximately 58.9%, which is about 1.7 points above the prior cohort. Read this movement as largely cohort-mix driven and descriptive only, not a causal or ship claim.

Collaborator-invite reminder
We will not run the proposed reminder experiment. The eligible population is 112 accounts versus an approximately 892-account requirement for the proposed renewal effect. The completed renewal analysis remains descriptive; we will not substitute invite rate for the renewal question or relax support-load, unsubscribe, or stabilization requirements to force a test into the quarter.

Lifecycle operations
The lifecycle QA and operations contractor runs January 15 through February 23 under Ines at a $23,180 cap, leaving $820 uncommitted in the $24,000 Q1 Growth envelope. The as-of preflight control has been repaired so the affected campaign can be held without freezing unrelated sends, and refreshed preflights now preserve reproducible recipient and exclusion records before release.

docs.title: Book-club discussion notes — first 20 minutes
docs.body:
# Book-club discussion notes

## Opening frame
For the first 20 minutes, use the three flagged threads to test how the narrator’s choices and the ending revise our understanding of the story. Keep the discussion exploratory rather than settling the questions too quickly.

## Discussion path

### 1. Protective or manipulative omissions
When the narrator leaves information out, what does the omission protect, and who benefits from it? At what point, if any, does withholding become manipulation?

### 2. The final train scene and the opening chapter
How does the final train scene change the way we read the opening chapter? Does it confirm, complicate, or undermine the expectations established at the beginning?

### 3. Whether the sibling relationship is repaired
By the end, has the sibling relationship actually been repaired, or have the characters only reached a workable new distance? What evidence supports that distinction?

## Two passages to revisit
- The opening chapter, especially the narrator’s first significant omission.
- The final train scene, especially the exchange or gesture that bears on the siblings’ relationship.

Use locations and short reminders rather than reading long quotations aloud.

## Closing handoff
“What did these three threads leave unresolved, and which question should we carry into the rest of the discussion?” Then hand the meeting back to the organizer for the remaining time.

## October 7 discussion

1. When the informal footpath is first framed as a planning failure, whose definition of failure is operating, and what assumptions does that framing make about how residents should move through the space?
2. When residents later describe the same path as adaptation, what changes in our understanding of the path, and can the failure and adaptation readings both remain plausible?
3. Why does the ending return to the crossing without resolving the competing interpretations, and what does that unresolved return ask us to reconsider rather than conclude?

## October 7 discussion recap

The group agreed that the informal footpath initially looks like a planning failure, while residents’ descriptions make adaptation a credible competing interpretation. The group remained divided over whether the unresolved final crossing is a weakness or the point of the ending. Keep both readings open rather than forcing a settled interpretation.

## January 20 discussion recap

The group agreed that the residents' hand-drawn water maps helped households find working taps and became genuine care infrastructure. Their practical success also shifted work onto residents after the city stopped updating outage notices. The group remained divided over whether officials' later reliance on the maps recognized useful civic knowledge or used residents' success to excuse institutional neglect; no single interpretation was chosen.

# Ginger-soy chicken

## Ingredients
- 2 lb chicken thighs
- 1/3 c soy sauce
- 2 Tbsp brown sugar
- 1 Tbsp rice vinegar
- 1 Tbsp grated ginger
- 3 garlic cloves, crushed
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- black pepper

## Marinade
1. Mix everything except the chicken.
2. Save 2 Tbsp before the chicken goes in.
3. Marinate the chicken for 2 hours, not overnight.

## Cooking steps
1. Cook until done, turning once.
2. Brush the saved sauce on in the last few minutes.

## Mom’s margin notes
- Add sliced scallions if we have them.
- For less salt, use half regular soy and half water — do not cut the sugar.

# October 21 growth operating review — evidence and boundaries

## Lifecycle ownership trial

The first governed lifecycle send evaluated 124 rows, released 119 supported rows, and held five rows. The completed audit was clean. The five holds were fail-closed safeguards, not releases.

Three rows whose release metadata was repaired were later given a fresh current-state check and released separately under a new governed decision; they were not retroactively approved members of the old send. Two rows with conflicting connector state remain held.

Friday's warehouse incident affected 41 rows whose `release_metadata_age` was null. Those rows remain fail closed while the engineering repair and verification proceed. Missing or conflicting state cannot be inferred from a prior export. The lifecycle trial's governed lane, weekly send ceiling, audit requirement, engineering-access boundary, and customer-correction stop rule remain in force.

**Pending:** the 41 affected rows require repair, verification, and a new current-state check before reconsideration; the two connector-conflict rows remain held.

**Boundary:** these early sends and holds do not establish a permanent ownership transfer or a lasting release policy.

## Expansion Assist second bounded cohort

The cohort currently has six actual exposures, one candidate suppressed before exposure because of active Customer Success work, one help-or-options request, and eight locked candidates awaiting scheduled checks. The cohort remains bounded by deeper integration use, a currently active qualifying human admin, a product-visible usage ceiling crossed within the prior 14 days, and suppression during active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. It remains capped at 18 accounts, with no more than three exposures per week, and the locked candidate set is not to be filled by relaxing eligibility.

There is no pipeline, forecast, or outcome treatment attached to these early exposures.

**Pending:** the eight locked candidates still require their scheduled same-day checks, and the exposure and outcome windows remain open.

**Boundary:** current exposure counts and one help request are evidence of operating status only; they are not a causal result, rollout decision, pipeline amount, or forecast input.

## Helio Start authority diagnostic

Through October 15, the diagnostic contains 33 unique enrolled workspaces. Duplicate export views are removed from the unique count while original rows remain available for audit.

The approved design enrolls the first 60 workspaces admitted from October 1 through October 28 and prospectively classifies each as external access or authority, product guidance, or mixed. Measures are resolution time, substantive repeat contacts, and support minutes. Summed human agent-minutes are the primary labor measure: overlapping human agents count separately. Elapsed customer-blocked time is retained as a separate field and is not substituted for labor; automated acknowledgements contribute to neither measure.

The conditional December 12 close requires enrollment to reach 60 by October 28. If it does not, the close waits until every workspace enrolled by the cutoff has a complete 45-day support window. Admission, pending-state, and routing rules remain unchanged. The diagnostic does not authorize an onboarding rebuild or changes to intake, routing, lifecycle email, or staffing from early cases.

**Pending:** enrollment and the specified support windows remain in progress, and the diagnostic close condition has not been converted into a policy change.

**Boundary:** the current count and measurement definition are evidence for the bounded diagnostic, not a broader operating-policy decision.

## Review principle

Keep current evidence, unresolved items, and approved boundaries separate. Do not turn any early result into a lasting policy, broad rollout, pipeline claim, or forecast claim.

docs.title: CS auto-nudge operator glossary — one page
docs.body:
# CS auto-nudge operator glossary

**Proceed** — The decision may proceed only when all five governed fields are within their freshness limits: external-system authority is verified yes for the connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action, connector authentication is authenticated, entitlement is active, a qualifying human admin is present, and no active Customer Success adoption or renewal work is recorded.

**Suppression** — Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses the nudge. This is a current-state operating outcome, not a stale-state error.

**Stale, unresolved, or conflicting hold** — If any required field is stale, unresolved, or conflicts with another downstream view, the system fails closed and shows the field-specific hold. Operators do not manually release it.

**Fresh-check rerun** — A stale field remains held until its source receives a fresh check. After that check, evaluate the decision again from the governed state; do not manually override or release the prior decision.

**External-system authority** — Connector-readiness state showing that the account or an available owner can perform the connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action. It is not permission for automated contact.

**Escalation ownership** — Owen owns routine exception-ledger interpretation. Ines verifies messaging-state alignment. Daniela owns engineering release and rollback controls. Riley handles customer corrections, incident stops, state-changing or ambiguous cases, exception-heavy decisions, and disputed semantics. Ines has no engineering release-control access.

The shared-state release is live, coordinated rollback remains available, and the legacy path is retained rather than retired.

Add these two de-identified side-by-side examples:

1. Active Customer Success work — A current source check shows active Customer Success adoption or renewal work. Final disposition: suppressed. This is a valid current state, not bad data, and it is not manually released.

2. Stale required state — A required field is outside its freshness limit. The decision remains on a visible field-specific hold until the source receives a fresh check. The system then reevaluates the decision and records the resulting disposition; an operator does not manually release it. If the affected field is external-system authority, it describes whether the account or an available owner can perform the connector's required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action. It is connector readiness, not permission for automated outreach.

docs.title: Helio Start internal triage FAQ
docs.body:
# Helio Start internal triage FAQ

## What are the three separate readiness checks?

**Helio admin proof** answers whether the applicant can legitimately administer the Helio workspace. Exact-domain proof can pass directly. A legitimate parent-company or IT-managed mismatch needs corroborating admin evidence. An agency identity cannot pass through self-attestation.

**Connector authentication** answers whether the applicant can authenticate the supported connector selected for first-week setup. A recorded yes can continue through the other checks. No or not sure remains pending and routes to Customer Success for assistance before admission.

**External-system authority** answers whether the applicant or an available owner can perform the connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action. A verified yes can continue. No or not sure remains pending and routes to Customer Success for assistance before admission. This is connector-readiness state, not permission for automated contact or other outreach.

Passing one check does not imply that either of the other two passed. Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state fails closed.

## What is ordinary product guidance?
When required readiness state is current and supported, a question about how to use or configure the product follows the ordinary docs-first product-guidance path. Examples include selecting an appropriate OAuth scope or understanding an ordinary supported integration step. Do not invent a combined readiness label for these questions.

## What are the possible triage outcomes?

### Assistance before admission
Use this when connector authentication or external-system authority is no or uncertain. Assistance for the unresolved connector-authentication or external-authority field occurs before admission. The applicant is neither admitted nor declined while the required evidence is pending. Connection or setup prompts that depend on the pending field remain held until Customer Success verifies the state and the system reevaluates it.

### Admission when every established condition is supported
Admission is supported only when every established eligibility field is current and supported for an under-50 account: Helio admin proof, simple deployment, first-week integration fit, a current entitlement state, supported billing, authenticated connector state, and verified external-system authority. Passing one check never makes admission automatic. A proceed result applies only to the evaluated decision and does not create blanket contact permission.

### Routed outside self-serve
Route agencies, unresolved ownership, manual billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, and other published refusal cases outside the self-serve path. Corroborating evidence may resolve a legitimate mismatch, but operators must not infer or self-attest missing required state.

## De-identified resolved example — owner-level evidence
An under-50 applicant had exact-domain Helio admin proof, supported billing, and connector authentication confirmed, but an outside IT provider controlled the selected connector’s required network allowlist. The application remained pending before admission and setup prompts stayed held. After the provider supplied a signed change record identifying an available owner and confirming that the owner could perform the required allowlist action, Customer Success verified the evidence. External-system authority then became verified, the workspace was admitted, and the held setup prompts were released.

This example shows that pre-admission assistance resolved only after owner-level evidence was verified. It does not change the general admission rules, collapse the readiness fields, or turn external-system authority into contact permission.

## Operator reminder
Keep the checks and their evidence separate. Preserve field-specific pending reasons, use a fresh source check rather than manual release, and do not turn verified external-system authority into outreach permission.

docs.body:
# Customer Success operator onboarding: five governed fields

This is a one-page explanatory aid based on Ines’s approved second Q3 message-state guide. It does not expand review-closure or engineering release authority.

| Governed field | Operator meaning |
|---|---|
| External-system authority | The account or an available owner is ready to perform the connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action. This is connector readiness, **not permission for automated contact**. |
| Connector authentication | The selected supported connector is recorded as authenticated. |
| Entitlement | The governed entitlement state is current and active. |
| Qualifying-human-admin status | A qualifying human admin is currently present. |
| Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work | Current CS work suppresses a commercial nudge. |

## Hold, suppress, and proceed
- **Field-specific hold:** Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state fails closed until the source is checked and the system reevaluates. Operators do not manually release the decision. Dependent lifecycle messages remain constrained by the held field.
- **Suppression:** Current active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses the nudge.
- **Proceed:** A proceed result applies only to the evaluated decision and does not create blanket contact permission.

## Decision-time scenario
- At 10:00am, the CS auto-nudge evaluates its required dependencies and receives a proceed result for that nudge decision.
- Before 10:30am, a required source becomes stale.
- At 10:30am, a lifecycle message must evaluate its own current dependencies. It cannot reuse the 10:00am proceed result as portable approval.
- The stale required state fails closed for the dependent lifecycle decision until the source is checked and the system reevaluates.

## Boundaries
Keep all five fields separate; do not create a combined readiness label. Proposed state-meaning changes, disputed interpretations, customer corrections, and incident stops route to Riley. Daniela retains engineering release and rollback control. This handout does not broaden Ines’s review-closure or lifecycle-send authority or grant engineering-control access.

docs.body:
# October 8 Growth leadership operating case

**Format:** 10-minute presentation, followed by 10 minutes of questions.

## Presentation plan

### 0:00–1:30 — The operating problem
Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, lifecycle preflight, and CS auto-nudge decisions depended on overlapping account state. Without a shared contract, differently timed downstream views could create ambiguous handoffs and unsupported decisions. The contract solved that operating problem without expanding Lifecycle Systems beyond those four named consumers.

### 1:30–4:00 — The shared contract
Keep five fields separately governed:
1. External-system authority
2. Connector authentication
3. Entitlement
4. Qualifying-human-admin status
5. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work

Each field has a source owner, as-of time, and freshness limit. Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state fails closed as a visible field-specific hold. Current active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses a nudge.

### 4:00–6:30 — A few locked Q3 proof points
- 1,362 unique CS auto-nudge decisions.
- 57 field-specific holds.
- No governed-field disagreement.
- No customer correction.
- One bounded pre-breach source-age intervention.

Interpretation boundary: this is operating evidence, not causal evidence. One pre-breach intervention does not establish mature reliability.

### 6:30–9:00 — The September 24 handoff decision
- Ines independently closes only routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and owns related routine operator guidance when the five field meanings remain unchanged, state is current and consistent, views agree, and no higher-risk issue is present.
- Owen retains routine CS auto-nudge operating explanation and the exception ledger.
- Riley retains disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer corrections, incident stops, state-changing, ambiguous, exception-heavy matters, and executive claims.
- Daniela retains engineering release and rollback control; Ines has no engineering release-control access.

### 9:00–10:00 — What did not change
The decision does not grant Ines closure or approval authority for Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, or lifecycle preflight. It does not change lifecycle-send release authority, add a fifth consumer, or broaden Lifecycle Systems scope.

## Likely questions

### Why are holds controls rather than delivery failures?
A hold is the intended fail-closed result when required state cannot support a decision. It keeps the affected field, source owner, age, and disposition visible and prevents unsupported action. Source lateness can still be a reliability issue, but the hold itself is the safety control working.

### Why does the September 24 decision not extend across all four consumers?
The reviewed evidence and authority decision were bounded to routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and operator guidance. No equivalent closure decision was made for Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, or lifecycle preflight.

### Why is proceed not blanket contact permission?
Proceed means the required state supports that evaluated decision at that time. It does not authorize other outreach, and external-system authority remains connector readiness rather than permission for automated contact. Every dependent message must evaluate its own current state.

## Closing line
The contract improved handoffs by making ordinary work independently closable while preserving explicit escalation, engineering control, and the existing four-consumer boundary.

# December 10 board operating segment — pre-read

## Page 1 — Opening frame
This pre-read presents four separate operating-evidence lanes: Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls. Each lane has its own denominator, complete outcome window, supported interpretation, and exclusions. The lanes must not be combined into one growth number or used to imply unsupported revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast conclusions.

---

## Page 2 — Helio Start
The mature packet contains 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows: 61 paid-active, 11 canceled, six past due, and four on billing hold. The cohort produced $95,420 in gross billed cash and $89,110 in refund-adjusted collected cash. Account-level support effort was 20 minutes at the median and 70 minutes at the 90th percentile. Seven accounts exceeded 90 minutes, all involving external-authority or ownership assistance. No manual-billing, import, migration, or agency case entered the admitted path.

Priya’s December 3 decision is to keep Helio Start as a bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026, with no paid-acquisition test, pipeline target, or forecast credit. A capped paid-acquisition proposal may be reopened only after two consecutive mature cohorts each have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes and no unsupported case enters the admitted path. Any proposal would still require separate budget approval.

The decision uses the evidence as a combined operating packet: complete day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort. The 61 paid-active count and $89,110 in refund-adjusted collected cash are useful mature-cohort evidence, but they are not scalable acquisition economics, pipeline, forecast credit, or a one-number conversion gate.

---

## Page 3 — Retained-mid Expansion Assist
Across the two bounded pilots’ closed, complete 45-day windows, 43 actual exposures produced 13 help-or-options requests and nine expansions. There was no randomized control, so the evidence is descriptive rather than causal.

The cohort definitions also differed: the requirement that the product-visible usage ceiling be newly crossed within the prior 14 days applied only to the second cohort, while 18 of the first pilot’s 30 exposures had an older ceiling event. Current-state safeguards applied, but the observed outcomes do not establish causal lift.

Expansion Assist remains a narrow, behavior-based, state-specific retained-mid operating lane. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses a commercial prompt. The lane remains outside pipeline, revenue commitments, forecast credit, broad-rollout claims, and Helio Start economics.

---

## Page 4 — Pricing-page path quality
The completed Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test covered 3,286 organic pricing-page sessions: 1,639 control and 1,647 treatment. Among Helio Start eligibility-flow starts, unsupported-condition route-outs fell from 38 of 344 control starts, or 11.0%, to 25 of 352 treatment starts, or 7.1% — a 35.7% relative reduction.

Eligible-workspace admission completion was 43.8% in control and 44.1% in treatment. Account-level support time at the 90th percentile was 71 minutes in control and 74 minutes in treatment. The direction held in all three weekly cohorts and the stabilization cohort. No unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change occurred, so the attribution check was clean. The result cleared the predeclared path-quality threshold and both guardrails.

The path-separated design has completed its rollout to 100% of organic traffic, and the control has been retired. Existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing events continue to populate without a taxonomy change. The supported interpretation is fewer unsupported self-serve starts and improved funnel quality, not revenue lift, paid-acquisition economics, pipeline, forecast credit, or changed eligibility.

---

## Page 5 — System controls
The certified October 1–31 CS auto-nudge packet covers 1,026 unique decisions. Forty-one produced visible field-specific holds, and 985 proceeded or were suppressed using current state. There was no governed-field disagreement and no customer correction. No held or suppressed record received adjacent lifecycle messaging that assumed eligibility, and no rollback was used.

This evidence supports system-control performance only: required holds remained visible, otherwise decisions proceeded or were suppressed using current state, governed views stayed aligned, adjacent messaging respected the state, and no rollback was required. It does not establish revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or customer-growth impact.

---

## Page 6 — Claims-and-exclusions matrix

| Evidence lane | Supported claim | Required exclusions |
|---|---|---|
| Helio Start | Among 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows, 61 are paid-active; refund-adjusted collected cash is $89,110; account-level support effort is 20 minutes at the median and 70 minutes at the 90th percentile; the channel remains organic through March 31, 2026 | Seven accounts exceeded 90 support minutes, all involving external-authority or ownership assistance; no paid-acquisition test, pipeline target, or forecast credit; reopening requires two consecutive mature cohorts each below 5%, no unsupported admitted case, and separate budget approval |
| Retained-mid Expansion Assist | Across complete 45-day windows, 43 actual exposures produced 13 help-or-options requests and nine expansions | Descriptive, not causal; no randomized control; 18 first-pilot exposures had an older usage-ceiling event; no broad rollout, causal lift, pipeline, revenue commitment, forecast credit, or Helio Start claim |
| Pricing-page path quality | The test produced a 35.7% relative reduction in unsupported-condition route-outs, passed both guardrails, had a clean attribution check, and completed a 100% organic rollout | Supports fewer unsupported-path starts only; no revenue lift, paid-acquisition economics, pipeline, forecast, eligibility change, or cross-lane growth claim |
| System controls | The October packet supports visible field-specific holds, current-state decisions, governed-field agreement, adjacent-message alignment, no customer correction, and no rollback | System-control performance only; no revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or customer-growth interpretation |

The four lanes remain separate. Their denominators and outcome windows are not interchangeable, and they must not be combined into one growth number.

docs.body:
# Riley Tanaka — 2026 year-end self-review working draft

**First draft submitted:** October 16, 2026

## 1. Evidence-grounded contributions

I strengthened Helio’s quarterly operating-evidence process by keeping each lane tied to its own denominator or exact coverage dates, complete outcome window where applicable, measurement limits, exclusions, source ownership, reliability evidence, and claim boundary. In Q1, I kept Helio Start outside the approved package when its required cohort dates were missing, while the three complete lanes moved forward with bounded claims. When the date gap was later resolved, I preserved the decision history rather than reopening the approved Q1 package. In Q2, I again kept the 39-of-50 day-7 Helio Start result out of growth and forecast claims because complete day-90 paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort were not yet available.

When the closed 50-workspace Helio Start paid cohort matured, I kept the result descriptive: 37 paid-active workspaces, $56,230 in refund-adjusted collected cash, 104 minutes of support effort at the 90th percentile, and seven of 50 workspaces above 90 minutes. Paid traffic stayed off, no second Q3 batch opened, and no pipeline or forecast credit was assigned. I treated source completeness as necessary evidence, not as authorization for another commercial decision.

I also supported the organic authority pre-setup checklist release while preserving the existing eligibility, route, lifecycle-suppression behavior, governed state meanings, and paid-acquisition status. At the October 14 review, Owen and Customer Success reported on 92 newly admitted organic Helio Start workspaces. Twenty-eight received the checklist because their selected connector required an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action and their external-authority state was current and verified yes; five requested ordinary setup assistance. The review found no eligibility or route mismatch, lifecycle-suppression issue, paid-source traffic, or unsupported admission. Because there was no randomized control, I kept the checklist in organic onboarding without turning those counts into an activation or support-effort improvement claim.

## 2. Leadership through delegation

That evidence discipline also shaped how I delegated routine work. Owen assumed the documented monthly sanitized-campaign-snapshot and board-source preparation workflow, then produced the July snapshot independently. Priya later granted him bounded routine source-completeness closure authority only when every required field is present, definitions are unchanged, named owners have certified their sections, and no cross-surface discrepancy exists. Missing fields or disputed interpretations remain incomplete and escalate to me.

Delegated preparation and routine source review operate within named authority limits and remain distinct from my retained responsibilities. I still attend and participate in routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews, while concentrating my review on exception summaries, unresolved discrepancies, disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, board readiness, final operating claims, and executive language. Owen’s authority does not include causal claims, revenue treatment, forecast credit, board-readiness decisions, or executive language.

I applied the same principle to the organic authority checklist. Ines may revise connector-specific instructional wording only while the required owner action, trigger conditions, and governed state meanings remain unchanged. Daniela must approve changes to connector-detection logic or release behavior, and any proposed eligibility or state-meaning change returns to me. This split allows routine wording work to move without creating a new line-by-line approval queue or blurring engineering and operating authority.

## 3. Boundary defended under pressure

The recurring leadership challenge this year was separating complete operating evidence from an authorized commercial or executive claim. The mature paid-cohort packet was complete, but completeness did not make it approval for another paid batch, causal acquisition or scale evidence, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. I held that boundary even when the headline counts could have supported a simpler but unsupported story.

I used the same discipline in the high-support review and authority-checklist work. The evidence pointed to a setup-sequence issue rather than a defective external-authority definition, so I declined an eligibility change. The checklist remedy remained non-state-changing and limited to admitted organic workspaces with the required connector condition and current verified-yes external authority. I preserved the October 14 evidence limits—92 admitted organic workspaces, 28 checklist exposures, five ordinary setup-assistance requests, no listed operating mismatch, and no randomized control—rather than allowing a useful operational result to become a broader performance claim.

## 4. Development priorities

My first priority is earlier escalation. Before a review begins, I will ask each source owner to provide the exact coverage dates and owner certification required for that lane. Any missing certification, date mismatch, or cross-surface discrepancy should be visible before closure review starts, not discovered during closure. I will define the checkpoint and escalation owner rather than personally reconciling every row.

My second priority is making staff and board language shorter and more decision-specific. I will state the supported claim, denominator or coverage window, and exclusions together, while continuing to attend routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews. The goal is to reduce avoidable late-stage rewriting without weakening the evidence or authority boundaries that make the conclusions reliable.

Across these areas, my contribution has been to make evidence usable without making it say more than it supports. I want to keep improving the speed and clarity of that work while preserving the distinctions among preparation, source closure, board readiness, final claims, and executive authority.

## November 6 calibration evidence — leadership through delegation

On November 6, Owen independently closed the first complete four-lane source packet under his September 24 authority. He closed it only after every required field was present, established definitions remained unchanged, every named owner certified their section, and no cross-surface discrepancy remained. I received his closure-and-exception summary without performing a line-by-line source review. This is concrete evidence that I can establish a bounded delegation structure, hold the authority line, and let routine source-completeness work close independently when the stated conditions are satisfied.

The November 6 close was a source-completeness decision only. It did not transfer or decide causal claims, revenue treatment, forecast treatment, board readiness, or executive language; those decisions remain in their existing owner lanes. I continue to attend and participate in routine monthly preparation and source-closure reviews. No 2027 role change has been requested or approved.

In H1, I increased Lifecycle Systems’ operating leverage by moving routine preparation, certification, and source closure into explicit owner lanes while preserving visible fail-closed handling and bounded escalation. I also maintained direct evidence contact through the quarterly audit rather than weekly line-by-line review. Priya approved one high-intent paid-search test with an $8,000 budget cap and a 25-admission cap. Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and assisted-routing rules remained unchanged. I held those boundaries through launch and execution and, with Daniela, closed the test on May 17 when it reached 25 admitted workspaces after $7,640 in spend. My development edge is to leave owner-ready work with its owner. I can add value by setting clear boundaries, testing whether the system works, and entering when an actual decision trigger appears. - Prepaid: $48,000 for a noncancelable 12-month commitment, except for uncured material breach.
- Monthly payments: twelve payments of $4,400, totaling $52,800, for the same noncancelable 12-month commitment. Monthly billing is not cancel-anytime and provides no convenience termination.
- Support tier, data-retention term, and service scope are identical.
- Shared allowance: 2,000,000 messages per month.
- Overage: $0.85 per 1,000 messages above the allowance, billed monthly.
- Post-term renewal: then-current pricing with 60 days' advance notice.

## Usage headroom
- Highest observed complete month: 1.79 million messages, leaving 210,000 messages of headroom.
- Approved planned peak: below 1.90 million messages, leaving at least 100,000 messages of headroom.
- A 100,000-message overage would cost $85.

## Decision table clarification

| Decision field | $48,000 prepaid | Twelve $4,400 monthly payments |
|---|---|---|
| Total payment | $48,000 | $52,800 |
| Service commitment | 12 months; termination only for uncured material breach | Same 12-month commitment; termination only for uncured material breach |
| Convenience termination | None | None — monthly billing does not provide convenience termination or cancel-anytime rights |
| Support, data retention, and service scope | Identical | Identical |
| Post-term renewal | Then-current pricing with 60 days' advance notice | Then-current pricing with 60 days' advance notice |

## Final selection and execution
**Final selection — authorized reviewers:** $48,000 prepaid option.

**Execution status:** Procurement verified that the final order form matched the approved commercial terms, and the authorized reviewer executed the prepaid 12-month renewal before the July 30 deadline. Monthly billing was not selected. The payment-shape matter is closed.

The executed order form adds no convenience termination and makes no change to the support tier, data-retention term, service scope, two-million-message monthly allowance, overage pricing, post-term renewal notice, or operating authority. All previously documented operating and authority boundaries remain unchanged. The operating recommendation itself was not procurement, legal, security, or engineering approval.

docs.title: Favorable estimate, no rollout — August method example
docs.body:
# Favorable estimate, no rollout

1. **Denominator** — The primary decision read was the completed 21-day powered window. The August 3–9 stabilization cohort contained 8,302 assigned sessions.

2. **Effect size** — The powered estimate was 12.0% in control versus 12.6% in treatment: a favorable difference of 0.6 percentage points.

3. **Confidence interval** — The powered estimate’s 95% confidence interval was 0.1 to 1.1 percentage points.

4. **Minimum-effect rule** — The predeclared minimum effect was 0.8 percentage points. A statistically positive estimate did not clear that decision threshold because the observed 0.6-point effect was smaller.

5. **Stabilization result** — The stabilization cohort read 12.1% in control versus 12.5% in treatment: a 0.4-point difference with a 95% confidence interval of -0.3 to 1.1 points. It weakened rather than strengthened the rollout case.

6. **Conclusion** — Close the completed method run without rollout. This example teaches minimum-effect and stabilization discipline and does not reopen the experiment.

# Incomplete-setup reminder — operator quick reference

- **Display:** Display only to a qualifying human admin when workspace setup remains incomplete, entitlement is current and active, and no current Customer Success adoption or renewal work exists.
- **Suppression:** Current active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses the reminder.
- **Visible hold:** Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state creates a visible hold. A held record is not a queued delivery.
- **Fresh reevaluation:** Every possible display requires a fresh evaluation, including after a state refresh or other state change. A refresh does not automatically send or display the reminder; the record must satisfy all current display conditions when reevaluated.
- **Monitoring:** Keep visible held-record monitoring active. Source-age alerts remain routed to Daniela and the named source owners.

- **Rollback:** Daniela retains rollback control by disabling the reminder flag.

Riley's August 9 replacement-evidence rule remains due.

Completed replacement-evidence rule: backend application creation may replace an impaired front-end signup event in operating reporting only when the signup flow has been independently verified as functional, the front-end impairment has a bounded interval and documented cause, backend creation uses the same workspace-level population for that interval, and the dashboard retains an explicit annotation. Retroactive browser events must never be fabricated. If these conditions are not met, the interval remains unresolved rather than being silently filled.

## Engineering inputs and limits — pending approval

Daniela's team can provide a read-only release-metadata export by 7:00am on weekdays and can flag connector-state incidents within 15 minutes of confirmation. Engineering cannot grant Ines write access to release controls and cannot guarantee a clean connector-state signal during an unresolved incident.

The proposal remains fail-closed: missing, stale, or conflicting inputs require a send hold. Priya's approval is still pending, so this proposed 30-day trial remains inactive.

## Proposed operating limits — pending approval

Add these measurable limits to the proposed 30-day lifecycle pre-send trial:
- No more than three sends per week during the trial.
- Complete and document an audit within 24 hours after every send.
- Automatically stop the trial if any send requires a customer correction.

These limits do not change the existing engineering boundaries or fail-closed send-hold conditions. Priya's approval is still pending, so the proposal remains inactive.

Two final proposed boundaries for Priya's decision:

- The incident-affected trial-ending automation cannot be the first send governed by the proposed 30-day ownership trial.
- No first candidate may occur less than 48 hours after a relevant production release.

The ownership trial remains inactive pending Priya's decision. These boundaries are proposed additions, not approval to begin the trial.

## December 9 review update

- The account owner explained that 26 contractor seats will roll off on December 31.
- The core team continues using its existing integrations.
- Acme requested renewal pricing at 85 seats and 110 seats.
- Acme has not committed to either renewal quantity.
- Customer Success owns the renewal discussion.

The contractor-seat explanation is seasonal seat cleanup, not evidence of product disengagement. Do not characterize the request as an expansion or contraction before Acme chooses a renewal quantity.

## Preview results and remaining release gate

Ines and Daniela completed the required preview matrix.

- Monthly workspace digest: the value is already trimmed before `default` is applied, and the template renders correctly for whitespace-only, null, and populated company-name states.
- Renewal reminder: loses its fallback company label under Customer.io's announced January 15 behavior.
- Integration summary: loses its fallback company label under Customer.io's announced January 15 behavior.

Remaining gate: Daniela owns the required template-code changes. Ines is holding the renewal reminder and integration summary out of January scheduling until corrected previews pass. The engineering fix is not complete, and neither affected template returns to scheduling before the corrected preview evidence is reviewed.

## December 16 quote update

Acme asks Customer Success to keep the 110-seat quote available through January 10 while Acme audits contractor access. Acme also wants the 85-seat quote preserved for comparison.

Acme says the 84-user count still appears to represent its active core team, but it has made no commitment to a renewal quantity. Customer Success remains the commercial owner of the renewal discussion.

The contractor-seat cleanup remains seasonal seat cleanup rather than product disengagement. No expansion or contraction has occurred, and no renewal quantity has been selected or committed.

## Concrete metric-discipline example and operational improvement

The December activation card displayed `125% — 250 / 200`. I intervened because the numerator mixed qualifying activation events with workspaces and the denominator was stale. The corrected view was 198 distinct activated workspaces out of 240 eligible workspaces, or 82.5%. The activation classifications themselves did not change; the correction changed the unit of analysis and denominator used for the conclusion.

Improvement area: before final review, I will specify the source, owner, unit of analysis, and decision boundary so late-stage interpretation does not change what the metric is claiming.

## Corrected preview results and completed release gate

Daniela completed the engineering-controlled fixes for the renewal reminder and integration summary.

- Renewal reminder — whitespace-only company name: `your workspace`; null: `your workspace`; populated `Acme Dev Shop`: `Acme Dev Shop`.
- Integration summary — whitespace-only company name: `your workspace`; null: `your workspace`; populated `Acme Dev Shop`: `Acme Dev Shop`.
- Ines validation: pass for all six corrected states.
- Monthly workspace digest: unchanged; it had already passed because its value was trimmed before `default` was applied.

The release gate is complete for the two corrected templates, and they can return to January scheduling. Daniela retains engineering release control, while Ines retains her standing lifecycle review and release authority; this result does not change that split.

## December 20 contractor-access audit update

Acme's first contractor-access audit found that 9 of the 26 contractor seats previously expected to roll off can be removed on December 31, while 17 contractor seats are needed through January 31. The requested third quote is therefore 101 seats: 84 active core users + 17 temporary contractor seats = 101.

Acme asks Customer Success for this 101-seat quote without committing to it. The existing 85-seat and 110-seat quotes should remain available through January 10. Customer Success remains the commercial owner.

This is a seasonal contractor-access review, not a product-engagement conclusion. No expansion or contraction has occurred, and Acme has not committed to a renewal quantity.

## December 26 101-seat quote update

Customer Success returned Acme's requested 101-seat quote at $23,634 annually, or $234 per seat-year. It has the same support terms and January 31 co-term as the existing options and remains available through January 10.

The 101-seat quantity is 84 active core users + 17 temporary contractor seats = 101. Compared with the 85-seat quote at $20,400, the 101-seat quote costs $3,234 more annually. Compared with the 110-seat quote at $25,080, it costs $1,446 less annually.

Acme has not selected a quantity. This quote is not a commitment, expansion, or contraction.

## Final improvement commitment

In January, before the first review of any launch, I will name the source, accountable owner, unit of analysis, and decision boundary in the working brief. If any of those is unresolved, I will make the gap explicit before recommending action rather than reconciling it after the review.

## January 7 renewal-option selection

Acme completed its contractor-access review and asked Customer Success to prepare the 101-seat renewal option at $23,634 annually, with the existing support terms and January 31 co-term. The quantity remains 84 active core users + 17 contractor seats needed through January 31 = 101 seats.

Acme has selected this option for paperwork but has not signed an order form. The renewal is therefore not complete. This seasonal contractor-seat decision should not be described as a product-driven expansion or contraction. Customer Success remains the commercial owner and will issue the order form.

## January 8 order-form issuance

Customer Success issued Acme Dev Shop's order form for the selected 101-seat option at $23,634 annually, with the existing support terms and January 31 co-term preserved. The quantity remains 84 active core users + 17 contractor seats needed through January 31 = 101 seats.

Acme has received the paperwork but has not signed it, so the renewal is not complete. The seasonal contractor-seat quantity should not be described as a product-driven expansion.

## January 10 prework inventory

The active inventory remains 31 lifecycle templates. Four templates do not have a documented accountable campaign owner, and six routine non-state-changing templates still lack a repeatable written suppression-check record.

Use the contractor kickoff to catalog the missing owner evidence, document the repeatable suppression checks, and identify gaps for the accountable Helio owner. The contractor does not assign campaign authority, approve or release messages, or receive engineering release-control access. Existing Ines, Riley, and Daniela authority boundaries remain unchanged.

## January 14 final readiness preview

Final production-template previews ahead of the January 15 Customer.io Liquid `default` behavior change:

- Renewal reminder: null and whitespace-only company names render `your workspace`; populated names render the supplied company name.
- Integration summary: null and whitespace-only company names render `your workspace`; populated names render the supplied company name.
- Monthly workspace digest: the template still trims before applying `default`; null and whitespace-only values render `your workspace`, and populated values render the supplied company name.

If production shows an unexpected rendering result after the vendor change, hold the affected template only. Do not pause unrelated lifecycle sends. Any engineering-controlled template change routes to Daniela; existing lifecycle release-authority boundaries remain unchanged.

## January 17 signed renewal

Acme Dev Shop signed the 101-seat renewal order form for $23,634 annually, with the January 31 co-term and existing support terms preserved. The quantity remains 84 active core users + 17 contractor seats needed through January 31 = 101 seats.

The renewal is now complete. Keep the seasonal contractor-seat context in the account record; this should not be described as a product-driven expansion.

## What changes / what does not

If approved, the Lifecycle Systems remit would create one accountable operating layer for shared state semantics, freshness boundaries, and cross-surface decision rules across Helio Start, Expansion Assist, activation reporting, lifecycle messaging, and CS-nudge dependencies.

It would not transfer engineering reliability or release controls from Daniela's organization, transfer Customer Success case ownership, make a shared state contract live in production, or alter existing domain authority before the organizational decision. Implementation values and production sequencing remain subsequent work. The proposal remains pending Tomás's January 24 decision.

## January 24 decision — approved

Tomás and Priya approved Lifecycle Systems as a formal Helio function beginning January 27, led by Riley.

The remit covers Helio Start, Expansion Assist, activation definitions, lifecycle email, and the state dependencies used by CS nudges. Owen leads measurement, definitions, and exception reporting. Ines leads lifecycle governance and message-state controls. Daniela's team is the standing engineering partner for event and state reliability. Riley retains the high-stakes cuts and the self-serve operating model, including support load as a first-class metric beside activation, but is no longer expected to reconcile every surface personally.

This organizational approval does not make a shared state contract live in production; implementation decisions remain subsequent work.

## January 31 week-one evidence

- The inventory now covers all five consumer areas: Helio Start, Expansion Assist, activation reporting, lifecycle messaging, and CS-nudge dependencies.
- Two current views operate at workspace level; the remaining views use account or destination units, so their exception counts must not be summed as unique customers.
- Three views do not expose a dependable as-of time to the operator.
- The January 27 lifecycle-export lag was repaired and the held rows were freshly rechecked without a report-level override.

These findings complete the first inventory pass. They do not establish a live shared state contract or settle the remaining semantic, ownership, and freshness questions.

## February 10 implementation sequence

- Owen's reporting specification will preserve each consumer's operating unit while reading the same five governed fields.
- Ines's consumption table will map missing, stale, or conflicting state to a hold; no consumer may reuse prior eligibility.
- Daniela's team must add a separate as-of time and freshness result for each governed field to the transport schema before the shadow replay.
- After schema work, the team will run a shadow replay and compare Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, and lifecycle preflight before seeking production release.

The February 7 contract remains ready for implementation but is not live in production. This sequence does not authorize a release or a report-level workaround.

## February 21 coordinated rollback rehearsal

Daniela added one coordinated consumer-mode switch backed by a preserved pre-replay selector snapshot. In the nonproduction rehearsal, Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, and lifecycle preflight all stopped reading the candidate feed and returned to their preserved selectors within eight minutes. Synthetic missing and stale records remained held throughout, and Owen verified that no prior true eligibility value reappeared.

This closes the non-atomic rollback gap only. The shared state contract remains not live: production replay evidence, complete operator visibility, explicit release approval, and verified release are still required.

## February 26 lifecycle-preflight visibility specification

Accepted as the implementation specification: for each governed field, the operator view must show the source owner, source as-of time, consumer as-of time, freshness result, and hold reason. Customer field values remain restricted under existing access controls. The feed-level timestamp stays visible only as a transport diagnostic and is not a substitute for field-level freshness. Missing, stale, or conflicting state continues to hold.

This accepts the specification only. Implementation evidence, production replay approval, release approval, and verified release remain pending.

## Evidence custody after closeout

Helio retains the complete handoff and the underlying archived release manifests and timestamped audits supporting the four records labeled `reconstructed`. Ines is the internal contact for lifecycle-risk evidence questions under the existing authority boundaries; this does not authorize retroactive certification.

The other two records remain `unresolved historical evidence gap — no contemporaneous proof available`. Current template configuration cannot establish what happened in those old releases. The former contractor retains no Helio-specific operating material or access.

## March 3 lifecycle-preflight operator-view staging result

Daniela implemented the accepted field-level operator view in staging. For external authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin status, and active Customer Success work, operators can see the source owner, source and consumer as-of times, freshness result, and hold reason without exposing restricted customer values. The feed-level timestamp remains labeled as a transport diagnostic only.

Owen replayed the nine January mismatch fixtures and synthetic missing, stale, and conflicting cases. Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, and lifecycle preflight agreed; each exception identified the responsible field; and no held record inherited a prior true value.

This is staging evidence only. No production replay or release has occurred.

## March 7 verified production release

The shared state feed is now live for Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, and lifecycle preflight. In the production replay, all nine January mismatch records produced the same current status and field-level timestamps across the three consumers. Seven additional records outside their freshness limits failed closed and remained visible as field-specific exceptions.

Owen verified each consumer's reporting unit, and Ines confirmed that pending-state prompt holds use the same governed timestamps as eligibility. Daniela's coordinated rollback control remains in place.

This release covers the three named production surfaces only. It does not make Lifecycle Systems companywide or mature, and it does not integrate the CS auto-nudge system.

## Live-evidence exception review boundary

Owen owns the routine exception readout, including records that are stale or conflicting and fail closed as designed. Riley joins only when an exception: (1) produces a different eligibility, reporting, or messaging decision across live surfaces; (2) reveals a disputed source owner or semantic definition; (3) suggests the shared-state contract itself is wrong rather than operating as designed; or (4) affects executive language or a high-stakes operating decision.

Riley remains accountable for those cross-surface and executive calls but will not shadow-sign off every row. This boundary applies through the current live-evidence period and does not prejudge the quarter-end result.

## Calibration addition — observable Q2 behavior
At each monthly operating review, Owen will lead the first five minutes by naming the denominator and unit of analysis, explaining the operational consequence of the supported result or exception pattern, and stating whether any issue crosses the existing escalation boundary. Riley joins disputed semantics, cross-surface decisions, and executive-language calls; this does not restore line-by-line review or claim that the still-open shared-state live result is complete.

## Shared-state first live operating result — March 28 close
Across the first three live weeks, the feed evaluated 638 records spanning two Helio Start reporting cycles, the March Expansion Assist selection, and three lifecycle preflights. Twenty-two stale or conflicting records failed closed. No record carried a different authority, active-admin, entitlement, or Customer Success-work status between eligibility, reporting, and messaging.

Owen owns the routine exception readout without Riley rechecking every row. Based on this operating result, the shared state contract is mandatory for new Growth and Customer Success lifecycle decisioning. Daniela will integrate the CS auto-nudge system with the contract next in Q2. The auto-nudge is not yet integrated, and this result does not imply companywide Lifecycle Systems maturity.

Accepted replacement language for the Q2 objectives:

## Shared-state reliability objective
Operate Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, and lifecycle preflight on shared current statuses and timestamps. Leadership will review monthly evidence showing the records evaluated, records outside freshness limits or with conflicting state that failed closed as visible exceptions, any differences in authority, qualifying-human-admin, entitlement, or Customer Success-work status across the three consumers, and the owner and disposition of each exception. The first three live weeks provide the operating baseline: 638 records evaluated, 22 stale or conflicting records failed closed, and no differing authority, qualifying-human-admin, entitlement, or Customer Success-work status across the three consumers.

## CS auto-nudge integration objective
Integrate the CS auto-nudge with the shared state contract while preserving replay, rollback-validation, and release-review gates. The existing nudge path remains in production while mapping and implementation proceed. Do not describe the nudge as live on shared state or switch production paths until the gates clear.

Implementation workback - these are checkpoints, not release dates.

- April 18: five-field adapter code completion. Daniela owns transport and source reliability. Evidence must show all five governed mappings without new semantics, per-field as-of time and freshness handling, and hold behavior for stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state.
- April 22: field-specific operator hold view. Daniela owns implementation and source reliability; Owen owns reporting semantics; Ines owns messaging consumption of shared state. Evidence must show current field values and timestamps, visible field-specific hold reasons, and external-system authority used only as connector readiness rather than permission for contact.
- April 23: internal dry run. Daniela owns adapter, hold behavior, and coordinated rollback evidence; Owen owns denominator and operating consequence; Ines owns messaging-state implications; Riley handles only the release boundary and disputed semantics. Evidence must cover evaluation, suppression, and hold cases, field-specific exceptions, and coordinated rollback readiness.
- April 24: controlled historical replay. Owen opens with denominator and operating consequence; Ines covers messaging-state implications; Daniela covers field-level hold and rollback evidence; Riley handles only the release boundary and disputed semantics. Evidence must include historical replay results, expected field-specific holds, and documented rollback evidence.

The legacy production path remains live. None of these checkpoints is a release. No shared-state switch may occur before historical replay, rollback validation, any production shadow, and release review are complete.

Q2 demonstrated evidence: In the April 24 CS auto-nudge replay, Owen independently opened with the complete 412-decision denominator, separated the 386 legacy agreements from the 26 differences, and correctly split those differences into 19 governed holds and seven active-Customer-Success suppressions. He stated the operating consequence and handed off before release semantics. Riley did not return to row-level review. This demonstrates executive framing and ownership of the standard evidence shape; it does not transfer disputed semantics or the release decision from Riley.

The corrected-lens remake has completed production and shipped under tracking number 1Z84R2X90377124518. Estimated delivery is Saturday, May 17, 2025. Delivery and usability remain pending, and I remain off the new pair until it arrives and is usable.

May 30 growth-focus evidence: Ines independently authored an accurate operator-facing explanation distinguishing current active Customer Success adoption or renewal work as a valid suppression from stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state as a field-specific hold. She correctly explained that a held decision waits for a fresh source check and system reevaluation rather than an Operations release, and that external-system authority means readiness to perform the connector's required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action, not permission for automated contact. Riley accepted the explanation without rewriting it. Riley's exception and stop authority and Daniela's engineering controls remain unchanged.

Accepted June 19 update:

- Ines accurately explains the difference between active Customer Success suppression and stale or unresolved holds. Active Customer Success work is a supported current state that suppresses the relevant message; stale, unresolved, or conflicting state fails closed rather than being treated as the same condition.
- In Q3, Ines will independently produce two operator-facing message-state guides using the governed field meanings. Each guide should make the supported state, hold condition, message consequence, and escalation boundary clear to operators.
- Routine governed message-state explanation remains in Ines's lane. Ines routes state-changing, ambiguous, disputed-semantics, exception-heavy, customer-correction, and incident-stop decisions to Riley. Riley retains authority over those decisions. Daniela retains engineering release control, and Ines has no engineering-control access.

Accepted revisions for the Q3 review: describe the CS auto-nudge migration as complete, with the legacy configuration disabled and retained only for controlled rollback. Frame routine Q3 operating evidence around complete denominators, visible fail-closed exceptions, and clear ownership rather than a promise of zero errors. Keep Helio Start in its actual operating state: a bounded-GA self-serve product already live on the public pricing page, with Helio Start reporting inside the existing shared-state scope and activation, lifecycle, support-load, and segment-economics evidence reported separately. Preserve the established lanes: Owen owns routine single-path reporting and exception explanation; Ines owns lifecycle governance and messaging consumption of governed states; Daniela owns transport, source reliability, and engineering rollback controls; Riley retains disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer-correction and incident-stop decisions, and executive claims. Do not reopen Helio Start discovery, beta, launch, or pricing-page approval, and do not add a fifth shared-state consumer.

Q3 evidence — Ines's first corrected operator-facing message-state guide was accepted July 11 without rewrite. She independently distinguished active Customer Success work as suppression; missing, stale, or conflicting governed state as a field-specific hold pending a fresh source check and system reevaluation; dependent adjacent messages as constrained by a held field; and proceed as limited to the evaluated decision rather than blanket contact permission. Riley tested it against the May 20 sequence of 12 holds followed by eight suppressions and four proceeds. This acceptance does not broaden authority.

July 25 Q3 evidence: Ines independently authored her second message-state guide, and Riley and Priya accepted it without substantive edits. The guide keeps external-system authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin status, and active Customer Success adoption or renewal work separate. It defines external-system authority as readiness for the required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action, not permission for automated contact. Proposed state-meaning changes, disputed interpretations, customer corrections, and incident stops still route to Riley; Daniela retains engineering release and rollback control. Ines now has two approved independently authored Q3 references, without expanded review-closure authority.

The requested one-page Customer Success operator-onboarding handout has been created from this approved guide, preserving the five-field separation, field-specific hold and suppression behavior, the external-authority/contact-permission distinction, and the existing escalation and engineering-control boundaries.

Pre-read for the September 10, 2025 Q4 Lifecycle Systems planning check. The meeting will cover procurement and onboarding readiness, preservation of the existing owner lanes, and Q4 work that remains outside contractor scope; it will not expand review or release authority.
